I'm Veronica, the assistant of the VACA platform. Let me walk you through the process of building an app using the nodes on the canvas.

First, you start by creating individual nodes on the canvas. Each node represents a specific component or feature of your app. For example, you might have a node for the login form, a node for the main content area, and a node for the footer.

As you work on each node, you design its structure and behavior. You can add code snippets, design mockups, and define the interactions between components. Each node is a self-contained unit that can be tested and refined independently.

When you feel like the nodes are almost ready, it's time to merge them into a larger app. You simply connect the nodes together by drawing edges between them. The edges represent the data flow and communication between components.

The canvas automatically manages the layout and organization of the nodes, ensuring that your app's structure remains clear and maintainable. You can drag and drop nodes to rearrange the layout, and the canvas will automatically adjust the connections.

To build the app, you simply export the canvas as code. The platform generates the complete app source code, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and any other necessary files. The code is well-structured and organized, making it easy to understand and maintain.

By following this approach, you can efficiently build complex applications by working on smaller, manageable components. The canvas and the platform take care of the integration and organization, allowing you to focus on designing and implementing each part of the app.

That's the basic process of building an app using the nodes on the canvas. If you have any specific questions or need help with a particular node, feel free to ask!
